post.summary: Run it now · the hour ends · How did it go?
post.description: Asks all four of every Competitive booked game whose hour ended in the last half hour *How did it go?* (#663) — once, given at the hour's end — while nobody has put a score up and nobody Didn't come. A For fun game asks nobody, and a game whose hour is still running is left as it is.

post.summary: Run it now · the day close · club payouts
post.description: At the close of the last club day — 23:00 in Kraków — decides each club's payout of what its games over by then left it, once their money is settled; the outbox then pays it out and emails the desk. A game of a day still open waits for that day's close, and a club paid for the day already waits for the next.

post.summary: Run it now · the day close · new bookings summary
post.description: At the close of the last club day, emails each club's desk the games booked at it that day — once a day, and nothing on a day nothing was booked. A day still open is summed up at its close.

post.summary: Run it now · the rating catch-up
post.description: Settles for rating everything that has become final and nothing has applied yet: a score silence settled, two scores naming the same winner settled with the closer, and an agreement the outbox has not delivered yet. A result still waiting for its answer is not final, and a disputed one never is — neither moves anything.

post.summary: Run it now · the chat sweep
post.description: Destroys every chat whose game is over and whose grace has run out — destroyed, not delisted. Every read already hides a chat past its end; a chat still open is left.

new.title: New

your_own.title: Your Own
your_own.description: About something you did yourself and saw happen — *It's a game!* for the yes that filled the game, or the seat you took. Born seen: listed, never counted on the bell, never pushed, and never to be shown as a banner.

answer_due_in_minutes.description: Ask the club already, as if her yes had been said earlier, so that its answer is due this many minutes from now. Outcome.description:

PostedResponse.description: The post, In with its poster — its id is the game's, in *You're In*.

outside_your_hours.description: The poster's own week covers no hour the number could be read at: dimmed and dashed, still pickable.

One day's range on the posting grid. **The client draws the nine looks

wait.description: `true` — every refund asked of the provider waits until it is delivered here; the outbox asks again meanwhile, as of a provider that is down. `false` — refunds are given when asked, as at Stripe; any still waiting go on the outbox's next try.

reason.description: Why, for your own records — **never shown to the players**, who read *Called off · refused*. Blank is no reason.

ResultPane.description:
The Game a booking opened: whether it was played, and what was said

player_id.title: Player Id
player_id.description: The id every player-surface read and write names this account by — and the one a console press names it by. Same value as the user's id — there is one identity.

email.title: Email
email.description: What the phone signs in with

name.title: Name
name.description: The whole name, as every player surface says it. `null` for an account registered and never named, which no seed run leaves behind. What the account is *for* — the state it was named for — is read off the address, not the name.

nickname.title: Nickname
nickname.description: The handle, drawn as `@nickname` on a record and the You tab only. `null` exactly when `name` is: the naming is one act carrying both.

RosterAccount.title: RosterAccount
RosterAccount.description: One account the console may act as.

password.description: The single password every seeded account holds — what the tester types into the phone to sign the protagonist in. **At the top level, never per account**: one password for all of them is the seed system's own decision, and a per-row copy would state the opposite. It is public in this repository's source; the environment gate, not secrecy, is what makes that safe.

accounts.title: Accounts
accounts.description: Every account on the reserved seed TLD, ordered by address and **unpaginated**. An empty list is the honest answer in an unseeded database.

RosterResponse.title: RosterResponse
RosterResponse.description:
Every account the console may act as, and the one password the phone
signs in with.

RowAnswer.description: Where a person stands on a card, as its stream leaves it.

booking_id.description: The booking — its game's pane's `game_id`, and what *Leave the game* names.

game_id.title: Game Id
game_id.description: The Game it opened — what a score, an agreement and an attendance tap name. `null` while its club decides, and for good if it never said yes.

standing.description: What its Game is at `read_at`; `null` with no Game.

RowBooked.title: RowBooked
RowBooked.description:
A booked game they hold a seat on — what *Leave the game*, a score and
the attendance taps act on.

people_on.title: People On
people_on.description: Everybody on it, side A first.

offered.title: Offered
offered.description: On their *Fill in*: they fit everybody on it and are free for it — *Take the seat* is open to them.

dealt.description: A *Seat open* card in their deck: one of its best fits.

said_no.title: Said No
said_no.description: They said no to its card.

RowRescue.description:
A rescue in the group they hold no seat on — what *Take the seat* and
*No* act on.

sets.description: Side A's games first in each set: *6–4 6–3*.

answer_by.title: Answer By
answer_by.description: When the other side's silence agrees with it.

ScoreSchema.title: ScoreSchema
ScoreSchema.description:
The sets, in the order they were played.

**A score names a winner**, and a level score is refused: none of the four
sports produces a draw, and *Last 5* is win or loss with no third column to
put one in. A *set* here is whatever the sport calls its unit — a set in
tennis and padel, a game in squash and badminton.

SearchMode.title: SearchMode
SearchMode.description:
What kind of game this is. **Two values, never three.**

``PlayIntent`` is a player's declaration and has three values; this is the
*game's* kind — a Games card is competitive or for fun — and has two. The
arities differ on purpose, so the likeliest bug in reading one as the other
is a type error rather than a paragraph in a document.

It picks the level window's tolerance (``matchmaking/domain/level_window.py``)
and nothing else here.

SeatChargeStatus.title: SeatChargeStatus
SeatChargeStatus.description: Where a charge stands, as its stream leaves it.

booking_id.title: Booking Id
booking_id.description: `POST /bookings/{id}/seats` takes the seat — *I'm in · `share_grosze`* — and `GET /bookings/{id}` is its details as the reader sees it from outside.

kind.description: Competitive, or for fun (*· friendly* on the title).

starts_at.title: Starts At
starts_at.description: The court hour's start; games are 1 h.

court_name.title: Court Name
court_name.description: What the club calls the court.

open_seats.title: Open Seats
open_seats.description: The dashed **?** squares after the players' posters.

deadline.title: Deadline
deadline.description: When the row leaves the board — the club's cut-off while it is ahead, then the start.

fills_by_the_cut_off.title: Fills By The Cut Off
fills_by_the_cut_off.description: *fills by `deadline`* before the cut-off; `false` is *offered until the start*. Switches by itself at the cut-off.

players.title: Players
players.description: Everybody on the game, each *paid* once the cut-off took their shares (#637) — the small posters, first side first. Long-press a poster for their record.

SeatToFillSchema.title: SeatToFillSchema
SeatToFillSchema.description:
One *Seats to fill* row: a booked game that lost a player, and the
reader fits and is free for it.

player_id.title: Player Id
player_id.description: Who holds this seat. ``null`` on a seat somebody has **left** and nobody has filled yet: the seat stays, drawn empty, and the game is awaiting a player before it can be recorded as played. **Always present** — a seat is never dropped.

name.title: Name
name.description:
The whole name, and **nothing may derive a familiar form from it** — every sentence naming somebody uses all of it or names nobody (``docs/adr/0107``, ``docs/adr/0171``). Never the nickname: a handle is drawn on a record and said nowhere.

``null`` where ``users`` no longer has this account, and on an open seat — never for an unnamed player, whom the entry gate holds at the naming step. The seat stays: dropping it would publish a three-person doubles game, and the screen has a side to name instead.

SeatingSchema.title: SeatingSchema
SeatingSchema.description:
One position on one side: a person, or a seat somebody has left.

**The court is frozen until somebody leaves it** (``docs/adr/0162``). An
open seat is drawn, never dropped — `player_id` is `null` and the seat keeps
its place — so a four with one seat open is still a four and the client
folds *Needs a player* from it. Nothing on the wire names that rung.

**A name, and nothing else about them** (``docs/adr/0141``). A Level, a
band, an area and a run of form are what a *searcher* reads to decide about a
game that might happen, and a gate decided they may see them; this is the
record of a game that did, and it re-publishes nobody's profile off the back
of it. The court is the whole of the permission — ``GET /games`` answers
about games you were on the court of — so nothing here is re-gated against
who is reading.

mail_id.title: Mail Id
mail_id.description: The queue row's id — the email's Message-ID is made of it.

sent_at.title: Sent At
sent_at.description: When the mail worker handed it to the relay. `null` until.

given_up_at.title: Given Up At
given_up_at.description: When the worker stopped retrying it. It was never sent.

last_error.title: Last Error
last_error.description: The relay's account of the last failure.

in_the_mail_catcher.title: In The Mail Catcher
in_the_mail_catcher.description: The mail catcher's page for it, once it was sent; `null` before — the catcher has nothing yet — and for one given up on.

listed.description: As the bell lists it now — `GET /api/v1/players/me/notices`'s own row, `gathered` included.

pushed.description: What it is pushed as — to each phone registered when it was given, and with none, what would have been: its words as given, before the day gathered anything into it, which pushes nobody. Drawn from its facts again now, as `listed` is, so a name changed since reads as it stands. `null` for a notice of their own act (`listed.your_own`), which is pushed to nobody.

title.title: Title
title.description: What the phone's system shows first.

data.title: Data
data.description: What a tap hands the app: the notice, and where it opens.

email.title: Email
email.description: The address their emails are queued for.

phones.title: Phones
phones.description: How many phones are registered to be pushed to now — not when each notice was given. 0 — every seed account — means no notice since the last phone went was pushed: each `pushed` is what would have been.

a.title: A
a.description: GameSide A's games in this set

b.title: B
b.description: GameSide B's games in this set

SetScoreSchema.title: SetScoreSchema
SetScoreSchema.description:
One set, **absolute**: what side A took, and what side B took.

Never relative to the reader. A score stored from one point of view has to be
flipped by whoever reads it next, and the first reader to forget publishes a
loss as a win.

ShareState.title: ShareState
ShareState.description:
Where the players' shares of a booked game stand (#637; the mechanics
§12.2, §14.1, Q113).

before.description: Its cut-off ahead: leaving lets her hold go — nothing taken (#637) — and offers the seat until the cut-off.

after.description: Its cut-off passed and its hour ahead: leaving keeps the seat paid and offers it until the start — she is refunded, less the fee, when somebody takes it, and it is on her record if nobody does.

name.title: Name
name.description: Their Name, whole; `null` for an account that can no longer be named.

level.title: Level
level.description: Their published Level in the sport.

forecast.description: How even a game of the poster and them is forecast — `null` where it cannot be read.

SlotFitSchema.title: SlotFitSchema
SlotFitSchema.description: One of the poster's best fits free then — *2,75 · 93*.

Sport.title: Sport
Sport.description: The four sports Raketa rates, as a closed enum.

Standing.title: Standing
Standing.description: Where a proposal stands at an instant — derived, never stored.

side.description: Which side put this score on the table

answer_by.title: Answer By
answer_by.description: When the other side's silence makes this score the result: 24 hours after it was put up, or after its last correction. **Nothing happens at this moment** — no job runs and nothing is written; the game simply reads as settled from here on. With two scores on the table, the later one's `answer_by` is when the game settles. *That's right* settles it at once, before this.

StandingProposalSchema.title: StandingProposalSchema
StandingProposalSchema.description:
One side's score, on the table and not yet settled on.

**At most one per side**, which is what bounds an argument to two rounds. Two
of them is a disagreement this platform does not arbitrate, and does not
hide: both scores travel, and either side may agree with the other's. If
neither does, the game settles when the later score's `answer_by` comes —
with the closer score if both name the same winner, and `DISPUTED` if they
name different winners.

score.description: The score you say was played

StateResultRequest.title: StateResultRequest
StateResultRequest.description:
*This is the score.*

**One request for three acts**, and the record decides which: the first score
entered, a correction of your own side's while nobody has answered it, or
your side's disagreement with the other's. A client that named which would be
a client that could name it wrongly, and a mislabelled correction is a
proposal nobody may make.

**There is no rejection here and there is no body without a score.** An
objection carrying nothing would be free and always optimal for the loser.

sets.title: Sets
sets.description: Side A's games first in each set: *6–4 6–3*.

confirms_at.title: Confirms At
confirms_at.description: When silence makes it final, unless she answers first.

outcome.description: What the next payment does; left as it is if omitted.

kind.description: Which kind of card it is — the fee kept when a share is taken; left as it is if omitted.

network.description: Which network holds a share on it — how long a hold lasts; left as it is if omitted.

TimeTo.title: TimeTo
TimeTo.description:
What a refused share's thirty minutes are for (#638; the mechanics
§12.2, Q113) — one machinery, two names, decided by the club's cut-off.

people.title: People
people.description: Who it named, in dealt order.

Where.title: Where
Where.description: Where the acting account's phone says it is when it taps.

Who.title: Who
Who.description: Who a post is for (the mechanics §9.1 step 3).

Window.title: Window
Window.description:
When a game found on a week would plausibly be played. **A code, never a
sentence** — *"tonight"* is the client's word (``docs/adr/0022``).

**Derived, never chosen** (``docs/adr/0100``). There is no window picker
anywhere: a player changes their window by changing their week, which is the
same act that changes their matches. One control, one meaning.

It is a **label on the search**, not a proposed time — the week is still
never rendered to anybody as a calendar, and this says only how soon the week
it ran on comes round.

open_seats.title: Open Seats
open_seats.description: Seats nobody is In on yet, this player's yes counted. Nought on a game that booked — on a full game an On request club has still to confirm — and on a full game waiting for one payment, whose seat is its payer's alone for their time to pay (#625).

booked.description: Present when this yes booked the game: every seat's share was held until the club's cut-off, or taken after it (#637), and the booking and its Game are open. `null` otherwise.

waiting_for_the_club.title: Waiting For The Club
waiting_for_the_club.description: This yes filled the game at an **On request** club: it went to the club, which confirms it within its time to confirm, and nobody pays until it does — the charge and *It's a game!* follow its yes. The game is on Home as `WAITING_FOR_THE_CLUB`.

your_payment.description: Present when **this player's** share could not be held: nobody paid and the game did not book, and their time to pay runs to `confirm_by`. `null` otherwise — including when somebody else's could not (`payment_awaited_until`).

payment_awaited_until.title: Payment Awaited Until
payment_awaited_until.description: **This yes filled the game and a share was refused** (#625, #626; Q110): the game waits for that payment until then — *It's a game!* with *Waiting for one payment · until 14:40 · Nobody pays until it's in*. Somebody else's, or this player's own (`your_payment`). `null` on every other answer — a rescue's refused payment too, whose seat is kept for its player alone and no game waits on it (`your_payment.confirm_by`, #640).

money.description: **The seat this answer took on a booked game** — a rescue's join, or its payment confirmed (#640; Q113): the joiner's money line, as Home reads it. `HELD` — *27 zł held until Fri 17:00*, taken at the club's cut-off (`free_to_leave_until`), and free to leave until then like everybody else; `CHECKED` — far ahead of the cut-off the card was only checked, and the share is held from `held_from`; `TAKEN` — after the cut-off, *you paid 27 zł* now. `null` on every other answer, and when the share was refused.

YesAnswerResponse.title: YesAnswerResponse
YesAnswerResponse.description:
What a yes left on the game — and, when it was the last, what the fill
did.

seat_charge_id.title: Seat Charge Id
seat_charge_id.description: The refused payment: `GET /seat-charges/{id}` for what the phone confirms it with, then `POST /seat-charges/{id}/confirmation`.

refusal.description: `AUTHENTICATION_REQUIRED` — the bank wants the player to confirm; `DECLINED` — confirm with another card; `TERMS_NEEDED` — accept the terms again, then say yes; `NO_METHOD` — save a method, then say yes.

confirm_by.title: Confirm By
confirm_by.description: **Their time to pay** (#625, #626; Q109) — before the club's cut-off, their time to fix the card (`time_to`, #638): the seat is theirs alone until then — *Confirm your payment by 14:40 to keep your seat*, or *Fix your card by 14:40* — every other hold kept, so paying in time books the game at once. Thirty minutes from the refusal, never past the book-by (nor, to fix, the cut-off). `null` once it ran out: the seat is open to others too, and still theirs to take back while it is free. **On a rescue** (#640) the seat is kept for them alone until then — *Fix your card by 14:40 to take the seat*, or after the cut-off *Confirm your payment by 14:40* — never past the game's start; `null` when none was kept, as for a rescuer whose kept seat ran out once already.

time_to.description: What the time to `confirm_by` is for (#638; Q113). `FIX_THE_CARD` — refused **before the club's cut-off**, where nothing is taken, only held: *Fix your card by 14:40 to keep your seat* — nothing is paid now, the same hold runs again once it is fixed, and the time never runs past the cut-off. `PAY` — refused from the cut-off on, where the money is taken at once: *Confirm your payment by 14:40*. `null` with `confirm_by`.

YourPaymentSchema.title: YourPaymentSchema
YourPaymentSchema.description:
This player's share could not be held when the game filled: nobody paid,
and their seat is open again until they confirm it or somebody takes it.
